scope: One previously identified failure case VP027; eight evenly spaced actual video frames per arm. Existing completed outputs only. Not a suite-level frequency estimate or retrained ablation.
matched_inputs: Caption, seed42 and resolved first-frame path are identical across versions. The two literal canvas paths are symlinks to the same file, with exactly equal RGB pixels.

observations.Wan_LoRA400: Hands and dough remain clear; visible changes in hand placement and dough shaping over sampled frames. SA4 PC5.
observations.R1_400: Hands/dough remain clear; sampled hand and dough changes are much smaller than native LoRA400. SA4 PC5.
observations.R10A_original400: Hands/dough stay clear but pose and dough are nearly unchanged across sampled frames. SA4 PC4.
observations.R11B400_normal: Strong repeating texture appears by frame11; hands/dough no longer recognizable by frame22 and remaining sampled frames. SA4 PC4.
observations.R11B400_request_memory_off: Same checkpoint and inputs, only request branch disabled. Clear hands/dough retained with substantial contact and reshaping; some finger/motion blur and uneven dough surface remain. SA4 PC4.
observations.R11B400_no_c: All physical/request injection disabled on same checkpoint; clear hands/dough with visible finger/hand movement. SA4 PC4.

decisions: The R11B independent request write is causally implicated in this case's catastrophic visual degradation: switching it off restores recognizable generation while retaining physical fusion. This supports removing this specific branch, not rejecting every possible semantic architecture.
Identical SA4/PC4 ratings for normal, request-off and no-C miss large real visual differences; keep raw benchmark scores but require paired visual review before adoption.

Original R10A has a process-execution weakness in this example even without API data or the R11B request branch. R12A current-state read/write addresses a distinct physical-fusion mechanism; benefit remains unmeasured.
Do not blame global VAE geometry, precision, missing caption, or all native generation for this case: matched native/R1 outputs retain a clear scene.
